form_behavior_no_key.description: Without a saved key, E/F text is appended to option_d as 'E. ...' / 'F. ...' and no correct_option radio is ticked.

must_not: The header-only preamble becomes a num:null question
Any question raises 'a letter appears twice (merged questions?)'
Q20 raises any missing-option or duplicate-letter flag
Q20 options are merged or dropped
An answer/key is invented when no key is present
Spelling errors outside FIXES are silently corrected (convenant, Raphel, centirion, Nasareth, Capernanm, batist, recieved)
E/F text is dropped at parse time instead of being exposed in e/f
notes: The source requires 40 queued items numbered 1-40, year 2021, and subject inference via the CRK alias.

The Q11/Q12 continuation line ('According to Matthew in the beatitudes,') is documented as staying at the end of Q11's chunk, but qwen-2 §7 calls this unresolved/unconfirmed as desirable, so no assertion is made about it here.

Questions with E options are listed in questions_with_e. The documented no-key form behavior appends E/F to D; with a key of E/F, D is replaced by the E/F text and D is ticked (fillForm/tick behavior, not parseQuestion output).
The current live subject list (archived 2026-10-23) contains CRS (id 14), so the alias selects it; the harness uses that list.
discrepancies: EC-41 resolved: the current live subject list contains CRS (id 14); the older snapshot that lacked it is stale.
EC-40 resolved as a hard server constraint: the archived PHP enforces four options and correct_option 0–3. The lossy overwrite of D remains a documented side effect.

The parse output is expected to expose E for the questions_with_e list across A/B/C. The documented form/tick output differs: trusted-variant-B computes radio values 4/5 for E/F, which do not exist, while baseline C maps E/F to D (value 3). This fixture is parse-only.
